note: Massachusetts has implemented the state option described in FNS 726.3, using 200% FPL as the categorical eligibility (CE) gross income standard. The OLG covers the key underlying concepts: (1) The Categorical Eligibility page states households become non-categorically eligible when income exceeds 200% of the CE Gross Income Standards; (2) The Simplified Reporting Examples page (Q2/A2) explicitly notes that elderly/disabled households 'are subject to the 200% gross income limit for categorical eligibility purposes' even though they have no gross income limit for SNAP eligibility; (3) BEACON automatically converts CE cases to non-CE when income exceeds 200%. However, the OLG does not explicitly connect the 200% CE limit to simplified reporting income reporting obligations. The simplified reporting case maintenance pages describe the standard gross income limit as the reporting trigger but do not describe the 200% CE threshold as an additional or separate reporting requirement for CE households. Workers could infer the connection between the two concepts, but the OLG does not present it as a unified reporting rule the way FNS 726.3 frames it. Additionally, the FNS note that the 130% reporting requirement still applies to CE households under simplified reporting (because it is a reporting requirement, not a gross income test) is not explicitly stated in the OLG — the OLG's treatment of elderly/disabled households as having 'no gross income limit' could create ambiguity about whether the 130% threshold applies to them at all.
